title: SSE capacity-aware resume negotiation and graceful reconnect fastpath
creator: Aisha Rao
description:
Problem: Clients reconnecting to long-running SSE streams experience either repeated full replays of output or permanent degraded latency when server-side capacity is constrained. Existing resume tokens are durable but not capacity-aware: they permit clients to ask for a full replay that the serving pool cannot handle at the requested concurrency, causing head-of-line latency and overwhelming KV-cache hotspots.

Goal: Implement a capacity-aware resume negotiation and graceful reconnect fastpath that: 1) allows lightweight client probes to discover resume feasibility before committing to a full replay; 2) offers a fastpath resume when the request can be scheduled without violating latency SLOs; 3) degrades to an efficient poll-mode or snapshot-handoff when capacity is constrained; 4) preserves compatibility with legacy clients via a V1/V2 header negotiation.

Scope: runtime changes (resume token leasing, admission-control flags, probe handshake), protocol extension (X-Redwood-Stream-Resume-V2 headers, lease TTLs, resume-feasibility response codes), client SDK updates (JS/Go quick probes and fallback), console telemetry + dashboards, and integration tests + canary rollout for runtime-1.22.
comments: 2025-01-12 - Spike complete: measured current cost of full-replays on dedicated pools (p50 latency increases by 38% under 1.2x peak). Notes in linked doc.
2025-01-18 - Design review with PM/Runtime: agreed on opportunistic probe (small HEAD-like event) with 3 outcomes: FASTPATH_OK, SCHEDULED_WITH_DELAY, FALLBACK_REQUIRED.

2025-01-24 - Implementation note: resume tokens become time-limited leases (default 60s) - servers return lease and capacity hints. If client reconnects with an active lease, server may accept a fastpath without re-queuing full backend work.
2025-02-01 - Security review request created: probing handshake must not leak model-internal metadata. Using opaque numeric codes and TTL-only hints. See links.
2025-02-05 - PR opened: runtime changes to admission controller and token manager (RFC placeholder). Needs review from storage team for cache eviction interactions.
2025-02-10 - QA plan approved: synthetic reconnect storm tests + chaos NGINX drop to validate fallback to poll-mode and snapshot handoff.
2025-02-14 - Code review feedback (Frontend): ensure JS SDK probe timeout defaults to 800ms and expose an opt-out flag for low-latency callers.
Next steps: address storage feedback, finalize API header contract, add canary rollout config for dedicated pools, update docs and SDK changelog.
acceptance_criteria: Clients can perform a quick RESUME_PROBE that returns one of FASTPATH_OK, SCHEDULED_WITH_DELAY (with ETA), or FALLBACK_REQUIRED.
Servers enforce resume-lease TTLs and expose capacity-hint headers; no sensitive model details leak in probe responses.
Under synthetic reconnect storms, system maintains p99 latency SLOs for active streams by gracefully degrading replays into snapshot handoffs or poll-mode.
JS and Go SDKs implement default probe with opt-out flag; existing V1 clients continue to work unchanged.
Telemetry surfaces resume_probe_success_rate and probe_latency in Console per-route dashboards.
Canary rollout completes without customer incidents on dedicated pools (canary config applied to 5% of capacity).
